name: Tradify
tagline: Job management for trade businesses: quotes, scheduling, timesheets, and invoices in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not exotic: customers, jobs, quotes, line items, time entries, invoices. An agent can produce a working single-operator version in a weekend, complete with PDF quotes and a week calendar, and for a one-person sparky or plumber that genuinely covers the daily loop. What it will not produce is the boring stuff that makes the paid version worth it: a real mobile app that works in a van with no signal, card payments, and a two-way accounting sync that your bookkeeper trusts. Rebuilding invoice numbering, tax handling, and reconciliation yourself is where DIY quietly becomes a second job. Solo and stubborn: build it. Two or more people on the tools: pay.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you log customers, create and send quote and invoice PDFs, schedule jobs on a week view, and log hours and materials against each job.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or cheap VPS to run it on
An SMTP account or email API key for sending quotes and invoices
Somewhere to keep the SQLite file backed up
Willingness to do accounting reconciliation by hand or by CSV export
whatYouLose: A polished mobile app with offline job access, photo capture, and GPS, which is where trades software is actually used
Two-way Xero and QuickBooks sync, so invoices and payments have to be pushed manually
Built-in card payments and payment links on invoices
Multi-user roles, tech scheduling, and timesheet approval once the crew grows past you
Somebody else worrying about tax rules, invoice compliance, and backups
moatNotes: The accounting sync is the real lock-in. Once a year of invoices lives in the system and lines up with Xero, nobody is migrating in March.
whyPeopleStillPay: Tradies are not paying for a job list, they are paying to stop doing paperwork at 9pm. That means the quote goes out from the phone while still on site, the invoice hits the customer before the van leaves, the payment shows up in the accounting software without retyping, and the apprentice's hours land on the right job. Every one of those is a small integration or a UX detail rather than a hard technical problem, which is exactly why a one-shot build feels close and then stalls. Per-seat pricing for a three-person crew is annoying but it is cheaper than the owner losing evenings to reconciliation.
notes: The CRUD is a weekend, the last mile is a business. Fine for a one-van operation that already has a bookkeeper.
prompt:
Build a local-first job management app for a solo trades business (electrician, plumber, builder). Single operator, no multi-tenant accounts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 14 App Router with TypeScript
- SQLite via Prisma
- Tailwind CSS, plain and dense, no component library
- PDF generation server side with pdf-lib
- Email sending via Resend, key in .env, and a NOOP fallback that writes the email to disk if no key is set

Data model:
- Customer: name, phone, email, site address, notes
- Job: customer, title, description, status (enquiry, quoted, scheduled, in-progress, invoiced, paid), scheduled start, estimated hours
- LineItem: job, kind (labour or material), description, qty, unitPrice, taxRate
- TimeEntry: job, date, hours, note
- Document: job, type (quote or invoice), number, issuedOn, dueOn, totals snapshot, pdf path, sent timestamp

Features in scope:
- Customer list and detail with job history
- Job detail page: edit line items inline, log time, running total with tax, status transitions
- Week calendar view of scheduled jobs, click to open the job
- Generate a quote PDF from the job's line items with sequential numbering per document type, stored on disk
- Convert an accepted quote to an invoice, copying line items and locking totals
- Email a stored PDF to the customer, record when it was sent
- Dashboard: unpaid invoice total, jobs in progress, unbilled logged hours
- CSV export of invoices with date, customer, subtotal, tax, total for handing to a bookkeeper
- Business settings page: business name, ABN or equivalent tax id, default tax rate, payment terms, logo path

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- User accounts, login, roles, telemetry
- Xero or QuickBooks sync, card payments, Stripe
- Native or offline mobile app
- Recurring jobs, inventory, purchase orders

Requirements: mobile-width layouts must be usable one-handed since it will be opened on a phone. Seed the database with two customers and three jobs at different statuses. Include a README with setup, .env.example, and a one-command SQLite backup script.
